use_when: The default for anything longer than a headline, and the spine every other formula sits on
structure: tension -> promise -> mechanism -> proof -> action. Five moves, in that order, each one sentence before you allow yourself two
example_vi: Buổi trưa chỉ có bốn mươi phút. Một tô đủ no tới chiều. Nước dùng nấu từ xương từ [giờ mở nồi], không nấu theo từng tô. [Số] năm bán cùng một nồi ở [địa chỉ]. Ghé quán trước [giờ] để khỏi chờ.
example_en: Lunch is forty minutes long. One bowl that holds until evening. The broth is simmered from bone from [start time], not made per order. [N] years of the same pot at [address]. Come before [time] and you will not wait.
fails_when: Any rung is skipped. Promise without mechanism is a boast; mechanism without proof is a spec sheet
plain_language_note: Tension is the problem the reader already has before you speak. If you cannot name it in their own words, you are not ready to write

name_vi: Vấn đề – Khoáy sâu – Giải pháp
use_when: Cold audience with a problem they have stopped noticing
structure: Name the problem in their words. Show the cost of leaving it. Then one solution, one action
example_vi: Bạn đặt cơm trưa vì không kịp nghĩ. Tuần nào cũng vậy, và tới chiều thì đói lại. Nồi nước dùng của quán nấu từ xương, một tô đủ tới hết ngày làm.
example_en: You order lunch because there is no time to think. Every week the same, and by afternoon you are hungry again. Our broth is simmered from bone; one bowl holds until the working day ends.
fails_when: The agitation is longer than the solution, or the problem is one you invented for them
plain_language_note: Agitate means make the existing cost visible, not manufacture fear. If the cost is not real, use a different formula

use_when: Warm audience who trust you but have not moved
structure: Where they are now. Where they could be. The specific thing that carries them across
example_vi: Hiện tại: mỗi trưa mất mười phút chọn quán. Sau: một quán, một món, quyết trong ba giây. Cầu nối: menu bốn món, không món nào là món phụ.
example_en: Now: ten minutes every lunchtime deciding. After: one place, one dish, decided in three seconds. The bridge: a four-item menu with no filler on it.
fails_when: The bridge is your product described generically instead of the one mechanism that actually carries them
plain_language_note: The bridge is the only sentence that has to be specific. The other two are the reader's own life

use_when: Any headline anywhere. There is no situation where two ideas in one headline is correct
structure: One concrete noun and one verb that only your product could take. No conjunction. Under nine words
example_vi: Nồi nước dùng bắt đầu từ [giờ] sáng
example_en: The stockpot starts at [hour] in the morning
fails_when: It contains 'and', or a benefit and a feature both, or an adjective doing the work of a fact
plain_language_note: If you can delete a word and the headline still means the same thing, the word was decoration. Do that until it hurts

use_when: The category is full of identical claims and nobody is believed
structure: Lead with the verifiable thing. Let the claim follow from it, so the reader concludes it themselves
example_vi: [Số] năm, cùng một nồi, cùng một địa chỉ. Chúng tôi không cần nói là ngon.
example_en: [N] years, the same pot, the same address. We do not need to tell you it is good.
fails_when: The proof is not actually verifiable, in which case this formula turns into a lie with extra confidence
plain_language_note: This is the strongest formula available to a small business, because proof is the one thing a big competitor cannot copy from you

use_when: One objection is stopping most people and everyone knows it
structure: State the objection more plainly than the customer would. Answer it with a fact. Then the action
example_vi: Đắt hơn quán bên cạnh [số] đồng. Vì nồi nước dùng nấu [số] tiếng thay vì pha. Ăn thử một lần rồi tự so.
example_en: It costs [amount] more than next door. Because the broth takes [N] hours instead of a sachet. Try it once and compare for yourself.
fails_when: You soften the objection. A softened objection reads as evasion and costs more than the objection did
plain_language_note: Naming the objection yourself is the cheapest trust you can buy. The customer already thought it; you are only proving you are not hiding

use_when: The product genuinely works differently and the difference is explainable in one sentence
structure: Everyone does X. We do Y. Here is what Y changes for you
example_vi: Phần lớn quán pha nước dùng theo tô. Quán nấu một nồi từ sáng và bán tới khi hết. Nên hết là hết, và nên vị hôm nay giống hôm qua.
example_en: Most places make broth per bowl. We cook one pot in the morning and sell until it is gone. So when it is gone it is gone, and today tastes like yesterday.
fails_when: Y is not actually different, or you cannot say it without a diagram
plain_language_note: A mechanism is why it works, not what it is. A non-marketer usually knows their mechanism better than any agency and undersells it

name_vi: Đổi chung chung thành cụ thể
use_when: An existing draft is full of words like premium, fresh, quality, dedicated
structure: Take each vague word, ask what observation produced it, and replace the word with the observation
example_vi: Trước: nguyên liệu tươi, chất lượng cao. Sau: rau nhập lúc [giờ] mỗi sáng từ chợ [tên chợ].
example_en: Before: fresh, high-quality ingredients. After: greens collected at [time] each morning from [market name].
fails_when: There is no observation behind the word. Then the honest move is to delete the sentence, not rewrite it
plain_language_note: This single exercise improves more copy than any formula. Every vague adjective is a fact that went missing

use_when: There is a real limit: a batch size, a season, a pot, a room
structure: State the limit, why it exists, and what happens when it is reached. Never a countdown you control
example_vi: Bán tới khi hết nồi. Nồi nấu một lần mỗi sáng, thường hết khoảng [giờ].
example_en: We sell until the pot is empty. It is cooked once each morning and usually finishes around [time].
fails_when: The limit is invented or resettable. Fake scarcity is the fastest way a small business loses a regular customer
plain_language_note: If you could serve one more and choose not to, that is not scarcity. Real limits are usually more persuasive than invented ones anyway

use_when: You have real customers and generic praise is not moving anyone
structure: One named-role customer, one situation, one measurable change, one verbatim line — all approved
example_vi: [Vai trò] ở [khu vực], ăn trưa ở đây [tần suất] từ [thời điểm]: '[câu nói đã được duyệt]'
example_en: A [role] from [area] has eaten lunch here [frequency] since [date]: '[approved quote]'
fails_when: Any element is invented. An invented testimonial is a fabricated person and it is the single worst thing this skill could produce
plain_language_note: Five specific words from one real customer outperform fifty five-star ratings, because specificity is what cannot be bought

use_when: Price is the blocker and the value is real but scattered
structure: List what the buyer receives, each with the cost it removes. Total the removed cost. Then the price
example_vi: Gồm: [món chính], [món kèm], [thời gian phục vụ]. Thay cho: [số] phút chọn quán mỗi trưa. Giá: [giá].
example_en: You get: [main], [side], [service time]. Instead of: [N] minutes deciding every lunchtime. Price: [price].
fails_when: Items are padded to lengthen the list. A padded stack reads as a padded price
plain_language_note: If a line in the stack would not be missed, removing it makes the offer stronger, not weaker

use_when: The reader must recognise themselves before they will read on
structure: Ask something only your actual customer would answer yes to. Never a question anyone would answer yes to
example_vi: Trưa nay bạn đã mất bao lâu để quyết định ăn gì?
example_en: How long did you spend today deciding what to eat?
fails_when: The question is one everybody says yes to. Then it filters nobody and reads as filler
plain_language_note: A question that everyone answers yes to is a statement wearing a question mark

use_when: Founder story, brand film, About page
structure: One place, one time, one action, one thing that changed. No moral at the end
example_vi: Bốn giờ sáng, bếp còn tối, nồi lên lửa trước cả khi mở cửa. [Số] năm nay vẫn thế.
example_en: Four in the morning, the kitchen still dark, the pot on the flame before the door opens. [N] years the same.
fails_when: You add a lesson at the end. The scene was the argument; explaining it takes the argument back
plain_language_note: Non-marketers write the best version of this, because they were actually there. Write it as you would tell a friend and then cut the first sentence

use_when: Every artefact, always
structure: Name the action, its cost in effort, and what happens immediately after. One action only
example_vi: Ghé [địa chỉ] trước [giờ]. Không cần gọi trước.
example_en: Come to [address] before [time]. No need to call ahead.
fails_when: There are two actions. Two actions is zero actions, because choosing is work
plain_language_note: 'Learn more' is not an action, it is a delay. Say what the reader physically does next

use_when: Any lifecycle or campaign email
structure: Subject states the job. First line delivers it. One action. Nothing else in the email
example_vi: Chủ đề: Hết nồi lúc [giờ] hôm nay. Nội dung: Hôm nay nồi hết sớm hơn thường lệ. Mai mở lại từ [giờ].
example_en: Subject: The pot finished at [time] today. Body: Today it ran out earlier than usual. Tomorrow we open at [time].
fails_when: The email carries a second announcement. The second one gets read by nobody and dilutes the first
plain_language_note: One email, one job. If you have two things to say, you have two emails — or one thing that mattered and one that did not

use_when: Paid social where the audience did not ask for this
structure: Open on the moment of change, not the setup. No logo, no title card, no greeting
example_vi: Cảnh mở: lát thịt vừa được vớt khỏi nồi, còn bốc khói.
example_en: Open on: the slice of meat lifted out of the pot, still steaming.
fails_when: You begin at the beginning. The beginning is where the audience leaves
plain_language_note: Start where a friend would start if they only had one second to make you look. Everything before that is your comfort, not their interest

use_when: A page has one conversion job
structure: What it is, who it is for, the one proof, the one action. Four elements, nothing else above the fold
example_vi: Quán bún bò cho dân công sở quanh [khu vực]. Nồi nấu từ [giờ] sáng. Ghé trước [giờ].
example_en: A bún bò shop for office workers around [area]. The pot starts at four. Come before noon.
fails_when: A hero image with a slogan and no statement of what it is. The visitor leaves without knowing the category
plain_language_note: A stranger should be able to say what you sell and whether it is for them, in three seconds, with the sound off

name_vi: Trang sản phẩm để quyết định
use_when: A buyer is comparing and needs the deciding facts, not persuasion
structure: The deciding facts first, in the order buyers actually ask: what it is, size, material, what it does not do, price, delivery
example_vi: Bốn món. Tô [dung tích]. Nước dùng nấu từ xương, không dùng gói pha. Không có món chay. [Giá]. Ăn tại quán hoặc mang về.
example_en: Four dishes. [Volume] bowl. Broth simmered from bone, no sachet. No vegetarian option. [Price]. Eat in or take away.
fails_when: The page persuades where it should inform. A comparing buyer reads persuasion as a missing fact
plain_language_note: Stating what your product does not do increases sales. It removes the buyer's fear that you are hiding the answer

use_when: You have permission to message and one thing to say
structure: One fact and one action, under nine words total, no greeting, sender identifiable
example_vi: Hôm nay hết nồi lúc [giờ]. Mai mở [giờ]. — [Tên quán]
example_en: Pot finished [time] today. Open [time] tomorrow. — [Shop]
fails_when: You add a greeting or a sign-off. In this format both are noise the reader paid attention for
plain_language_note: At this length every word costs the same as a sentence. Write it long, then cut to nine

use_when: Short vertical video for social or ads
structure: Second 0-1 the change. 1-8 the mechanism shown, not stated. 8-12 the proof. 12-15 the action, spoken and on screen
example_vi: 0-1: thịt vớt khỏi nồi. 1-8: tay múc nước dùng, cận mặt nước. 8-12: bảng hiệu và địa chỉ. 12-15: 'Trước [giờ].'
example_en: 0-1: meat lifted from the pot. 1-8: hands ladling, close on the broth surface. 8-12: the sign and the address. 12-15: 'Before [time].'
fails_when: Narration explains what the picture already shows. Then both are wasted
plain_language_note: Show the mechanism, say the proof. If the voice is describing the image, delete one of them

use_when: There is a genuine, checkable, new fact
structure: The news in the first sentence, dated and attributable. Context second. Quote third. Contact last
example_vi: [Tên quán] mở điểm thứ hai tại [địa chỉ] từ [ngày].
example_en: [Shop] opens a second location at [address] on [date].
fails_when: There is no news, only an opinion about your own business. No journalist will carry that, and asking damages the next real approach
plain_language_note: If you cannot write the first sentence as something that happened on a date, you do not have news yet

name_vi: Trả lời khiếu nại công khai
use_when: A public complaint is visible and other buyers are reading the reply, not the complainer
structure: Acknowledge the specific thing. State what happened, if you know. State what changes. Move to private for the resolution
example_vi: Hôm đó nước dùng hết sớm và bạn phải đợi. Đúng là lỗi của quán. Từ [ngày] quán ghi rõ giờ dự kiến hết nồi trên bảng.
example_en: The broth ran out early that day and you waited. That was our mistake. From [date] the expected finish time is written on the board.
fails_when: You apologise without stating what changes. Other readers are checking whether anything will be different, not whether you are sorry
plain_language_note: The audience for a public reply is never the person complaining. It is the fifty people deciding whether to risk you
